title: The Star Wars Holiday Special Comes to the Big Screen!
review:
Well, so Luke: This whiny dork is your father? Now I understand why Luke Skywalker screams "No! No! That's impossible!" so dramatically in 'The Empire Strikes Back'. I'd jump into a chasm too, if I knew my dad was this adolescent, miscast, Scott Stapp-lookin' wimp. (Casting Hugh Jackman or Alan Rickman would have made a lot more sense!) Whew! Well, George, thanks. It's been fun. Go write for Sesame Street now.

Everybody keeps hyping the battle scenes. Why? It's the battle of Naboo all over again, only in space. Yeah, the fire trucks were a nice touch; but who was who? And what the hell was all this fighting about to begin with? ...And who killed all the good writers, anyhow?

Annoying to the point of self-mutilation, Yoda has become! Backwards every one of his lines is. Jeopardy it is like watching. Get it, we all do! Stop, now you can! Older than your 900-year-old butt, it is getting. Enough about that, that is! At least 'Jar-Jar Binks' keeps his cake-hole shut in this one. That's about the only saving grace.

***Spoiler Alert*** The opening credits are yellow, and they slowly crawl away from the viewer in an almost pyramid-like fashion. Pretty cool!

title: Star What??? Revenge Of Lucas Arts $$$
review:
Lucas should feel shame for all of his wasted efforts beyond the original trilogy. Since the mid 70's, fans have waited with great anticipation for follow-ups to the first low-budget blockbuster that could have outlived history and possibly still will. Unfortunately none of the newest releases from the 2000's will receive the same regard.

What makes the original Star Wars such a great movie is simply the fact that very little money was available to make the film, and yet it turned out beautifully with a handful of no-name actors including a set-carpenter named Harrison Ford. In contrast, with an amassed king's fortune, Lucas returns to the public with video game graphics and a story line that suffers greatly as he tries to tie the new in with the old.

Granted you will find some cheese in the originals, but nothing like the poor direction, writing and performances offered up in the new series to include this less than satisfying finale. For all those who might believe that this film is a smash hit, Lucas has truly mastered the force and used the Jedi mind-trick on the public to rake in the cash.

Once again, contrasting the two series, Lucas had something to be proud of in the first creations of the 70's and 80's as special effects were costly and difficult to create with stop motion photography, miniature models and so on. With that, each scene required a lot of work and talent to pull off. All of these efforts are clearly obvious and result in a film series appreciated by millions. However, in the new creations, it appears as though a group of overzealous CGI programmers have slopped together a cartoonish video game with lots of bright lights and effects that dazzle the average carnival patron. Although the special effects can be considered interesting and do offer some marvelous characteristics, they are way overdone and are seemingly used to cover for a story that lacks luster and feels short with a lot of fluff in between. Though it is understandable that the new series needed to appeal to the latest generation, the prop graphics such as the ships and such are far more fantastic than those from a series that is supposed to follow.

The screen play and acting fall short too, as each of the actors including those well known with long successful careers, appears to be out on their first run with over dramatics and poorly written lines. Additionally many of the scenes including a hand-to-hand fight just a few feet over a lava river exceed the believability of this story, even in fantasy terms. As for the storyline and screen play, in each film both seem to be lacking any real consistency or the dynamics of a truly creative plot. In fact each story feels like nothing more than a stretch to get something out for a quick buck. Lastly, Lucas's attempt to create a series that joins the previous creations is weak and laden with inconsistencies.

In short, the latest film series including finale appear as a lot of eye candy with little else to offer. Unless you are a die hard fan from the 70's that doesn't mind disappointment and the over inflated cost of theater concessions, I recommend at the very least, to wait for this film on cable. Don't even waste your time and money buying or renting the DVD. It just isn't worth it.

title: Why do so many rate this movie 10/10?
review:
A 10/10 rating means this movie cannot be improved upon. This is the sort of score that should be reserved for the Godfather, One Flew over the Cuckoo's Nest and perhaps Star Wars Episode VI. The majority of reviewers seem to be blinded by the special effects and the reputation of this prequel and do not seem to understand that the acting, particularly of Ewan MacGregor, is hopelessly sub-par. There is no emotion or involvement in any of the principle actors. Whether this is the fault of a poor script or the fault of Christiansen, MacGregor and Portman it is hard to tell. I noticed this especially when MacGregor discovers that Anakin, a man he has devoted most of his recent life to training, is a sith lord. The level of surprise and shock that he must feel is barely discernibleto the audience. And don't get me started on his appalling excuse for a accent. I can only assume that American viewers are unable to hear the ridiculous bastardised Scottish nuances in it. However, Darth Vaders first few breaths were magical (until he says Padme - a name that just cant be said in a deep voice) and Ian McDamuid's performance was powerful and impressive. Samuel L Jackson was also impressive, doing much with the little he had to work with.

I can only wish that the viewing audience can see past what is clearly a lacklustre movie and that the hundreds of 10/10 reviews on this site represent a fanatical and unbalanced minority.

Sidenote: I actually met Ian McDarmuid in Edinburgh a couple of years ago, in a vegetarian restaurant, of all places.

Don't get me wrong this isn't a 1/10 movie more like a 5/10 but most voters have been submitting 10/10 and making a mockery of the whole rating system.

People that gives this film 10/10 is saying it's a perfect movie in every way. In my view their opinion is worthless so don't read their comments.

My opinion, it's OK and that's all.

In this film there is supposed to be a war getting fought. We see lots of lasers and spaceships but where are the effects of the war ? Everyone looks to be living pretty well from where I sat.

Bad Points: No excitement, no character building, shocking plot.

Good Points: SFX, good production, cinematography.

title: Episode III is a cinematic masterpiece!!!
review: I don't usually write reviews for movies and I don't like the insults that I've seen on previous forums. But when I have just seen a movie that I can't stop talking about and more than that has made me cry every time I have gone to see it then this kind of film deserves a review. My Dad took me to go see Star Wars: A new Hope when it was re-released in the early 80's and then me and him went and saw Return of the Jedi twice. I have been a fan of the films ever since. I have probably put more money in Lucas's pocket than I should. In Episode I yes Jar-Jar was annoying but I liked the story and even little Jake Lloyd as Anakin was not a bad choice at all. The critical reaction from fans on Episode I in my opinion is unfair. The same with Attack of the Clones, the romance between Anakin and Padme may seem a bit contrived but it needs to be told and come on seeing Yoda fight with a light saber even if it is a short time. Now on to Episode III which has become my favorite of all the Star Wars movies. I loved Empire but now it has fallen to second place. Revenge of the Sith is a cinematic masterpiece and I loved it. It was one of the most phenomenal experiences of my life. The light saber duels to Anakins dark transformation were wonders to behold. It was chilling, disturbing and overall just very tragic to see the domino effect that was put in place by Palpatine. Hayden stepped it up from Attack of the Clones. His portrayal of a tormented Anakin Skywalker was off of the charts. Also, unbelievable connections were made to Episode IV and the other movies. I don't care what box office this movie makes. Even if you are not a Star Wars fan go and see it. I saw it at midnight on the 18th and saw it two more times after that. Please go and see this film. It is well worth the price of admission. Thank you George Lucas for giving me some of the most brilliant motion pictures in cinema history. Thank you for Revenge of the Sith. This opinion can be criticized I don't care. I will stand by it till the day I die.

title: Lukas Has Completed His Journey To The Darkside
review:
This was the worst film comparable to even the lowest of B grade films.

First, CGI is not the answer to film-making or a great film. By saying that, this film is so overdone in CGI with little to nothing else to show that it is simply trash. By the way, please take the CGI added effects out of the originals, it only brings them to level of the current works.

Before proceeding I think it would be appropriate to grade the film on each of it's characteristics.

1. Special Effects 5/10 2. Acting 1/10 3. Story 2/10 4. Directing 1/10 5. Merchandising 10/10

What can anyone with half a brain say about this film that is really good? It did nothing to intrigue even children.

At best the special effects are it's greatest strength and that just isn't saying much. The reason is that the effects are obvious CGI and are over abundant, appearing as an attempt to make up for a poorly crafted story line.

The acting was absolutely horrible. I'm no soap fan, yet I would rather watch a month of straight soaps than ten more minutes of this finale. The only reason I use soaps for an analogy here is that the acting was at or below the level of the most common soap opera. I couldn't believe how truly poor it was. No excuse George! Additionally, at no point in the film could you get remotely involved as it jumped from place to place so abruptly.

The story was thin with little to almost no real plot other than Darth Vader is born. Everything in between was senseless filler and fluff just to get two hours of film. The story also leaves many holes and inconsistencies in the effort to tie the two trilogies together. Many of the scenes exceed even the logic of fantasy.

What else can be said that hasn't already been said? At best I can only ask how anyone could be so blind as to fail to recognize the garbage churned out here in this production? This includes not only the production team along with director George Lucas, but additionally the audience of those believing it to be some great work of art.

Understandably, beauty is in the eyes of the beholder, but even the most blind can tell a dog from a beauty-queen. This film definitely qualifies as a dog.

Merchandising??? It goes without saying that we have all made Lucas Arts rich beyond the standards of Donald Trump and Bill Gates. The question you might ask here is... "Why?"

In short, this film lacks a great deal on every level accept advertising and merchandising. It had a potential to be something great and close out a legend in film-making with a bang. Yet at best, it only lived up to the stereotype of sequels, where the sequel always falls a minimum of 2 steps below its predecessor. After 20 years and a few banks full of money, this one film should have been much better to say the least!

Oh Yeh... I Want My Money Back!!!

title: out with a whimper instead of a bang
review: it is a terrible shame that Lucas could not have brought on board people who could write and a director who could direct actors. the script is worse than usual with every line a cliché, the performances vary from good Ian mcdiarmid (emperor/palpadine), Natalie portman (padme) to average McGregor (obi wan) to the bad Christensen (annakin). And there is the main problem as we are dealing with the demise of annakin and the birth of Vader, the actor needed to have gravitas and authority, poor Haydn has neither and struggles manfully to fill the body and shoes of Vader but does not succeed. i am baffled by the response by both critics and fans alike that this is the best of the new trilogy, for me it is the most emotionless. there was no sense of story or character, far too many battle scenes, the one on the wookie planet had absolutely no purpose other than to get Yoda out of the way. or maybe as someone said after the screening to capitalise on the merchandising. anyway i shall see it again to see if it gets better or not

title: The Best One of the New Trilogy
review:
This 2005 film is the best of the newer trilogy. However it still has major flaws and a paper thin story. The actors can not compensate for a story that really is razor thin.

If you see the film "Rouge One" you will understand that film should of been this film. It would have been more entertain had this film focused on the building of the "Death Star". It also would have been great to see a better way the Anakin turn to the "Dark Side"

The one bright note is that Jar Jar Binks only has a 1 second cameo in this.

title: This is what passes for a good movie?
review:
I am no stranger to the "Star Wars" films. I have seen all six of them and even the infamous "Clone Wars" movie from 2008. This terrifies me. I can understand people claiming this is the best of the prequels, but then there is all that talk about how it is as good or even better than "Empire Strikes Back". How is this film that popular? I do not understand.

Let me start off with a few positives. This is the first film in the prequels where I have no questions from from the opening crawl and I understand what is going on and what is at stake and why I should care. Next, it downplays the romance element from "Attack of the Clones" and the dialog has improved quite a bit.

Now for the bad. The acting is terrible with the exception of Ewan McGregor, Ian McDiarmid, Frank Oz, and to a lesser extent, Anthony Daniels and Jimmy Shmits (two actors of minor/supporting characters might I add). Hayden Christensen does improve from his performance from "Attack of the Clones" but it all feels overplayed. Natalie Portman has a few good scenes but is overall bad in this film. Samuel L. Jackson is very monotone in this film, as is Christopher Lee. So with that, a majority of the main cast does not do very well in the acting department.

A lot of things in the film are over or underdone. Most of the acting and story is underdone, the ending and the dark tone are overdone. It seems like to be a dark film, Lucas believes that it has to be PG-13. I'm sure that is not the case but it feels that way. The ending is more like a soap opera season finale than the actual climax to a film series with a plot element like Padme losing the will to live and a race against the clock to save the babies.

A problem arises with the character of Anakin Skywalker. In the last film, it might have been understandable that he was whiny and arrogant as he was younger and less mature, but at this point he has been fighting the Clone Wars for several years and it has lessened, but only by a small amount. He still acts whiny and arrogant, claiming the council is holding him back from being a Jedi Master. And this is the guy we are supposed to feel sympathy for when he tragically falls to the dark side?

You have no sympathy for Anakin and thus, you do not want to route for him in this film. To make matters worse, it isn't even one of those things where you want to route for the villains instead. You do not want to route for anyone. If you do not want to route for any of the characters than the film is boring, plain and simple.

Once again, I have to ask: This passes for a good movie?

title: The force (and the prequels) can have a strong influence on the weak minded
review:
"A special effect is a tool, a means of telling a story. A special effect without a story is a really boring thing"

George Lucas - 1983

I have come to the conclusion that the casual American audience can only pay attention to something which contains childish humor, computer generated (over used too) eye candy, useless stylized fighting, pointless action and superficial story telling. This film along with it's two older siblings is a testament to how much George Lucas has truly become one with the money hungry Hollywood machine. I couldn't agree more with what Lucas stated back in '83 (see above). I guess he doesn't agree anymore or maybe he never really believed it.

The last three installments (dare I include Jedi too?) have felt more like Lucas saying "look what I can do" or "how can I screw people out of their money by playing off of peoples nostalgia or lack of rational thought." Starting with the special editions of 1997, Star Wars started to look more like Star Wars meets The Jetsons. Pointless robots with cartoonish voices buzzing about reciting clichés of days past ("how wude", "roger roger", "exxxccuuuuuse me"). The overuse of green screen compositing reminded me of the merry-go-round cartoon scene in Mary Poppins. Though the cgi Yoda looked a little better in this installment I still prefer the puffy faced, Homer Simpson mouthed puppet used in the Phantom Menace. The acting is skin scrawling with some of the worst dialog since an old ABC after school special.

I feel the the actors cannot be blamed for this mess. In fact I think that they really tried. I'll even go so far as to say that Hayden Christiensen (spelling?) and Natalie Portman have gotten a bum wrap for their performances. They had horrible dialog to work from in the first place. There really isn't much a person can do with "This is the end of you, master" and make it sound any better. I won't get going on the unbelievably sappy talk between Anakin and Padme. Don't get me wrong, I am all for character development and emotional storytelling but that dialog was just BAD. I don't think Fabio would even wanna be on the cover of a book containing that kind of writing.

I feel that George Lucas did a great job with American Graffiti but then again he had a cast of actors that were about to become major stars and household names (along with a lead that would later earn the Oscar Best Director). Star Wars was a great follow up but much to the denial of some, it was truly a case of the right time and the right place. But I do have to give him credit for that since it helped spawn the next generation of film makers. He started out as a rogue in the industry yet eventually became what he fought against. I think it happens with a lot of film makers, much like politicians, they go in with great intentions but end of being assimilated into the Hollywood system. I truly hope that since the Star Wars cash cow has finally ended he can get back to making more meaningful material like his more idealistic days of old.

In closing, if you're looking for bad dialog, tired directing, childish humor, dime store romance, flashy yet useless dueling moves, rejects from the Jetsons, and VERY excessive use of digital effects, this is your movie. If you're looking for solid character development, good twists, tasteful use of visual effects, and story telling above the 1st grade level, look elsewhere. I was very into Star Wars while growing up but have found that these last few films have tainted my appreciation. I'm sorry if I have offended or made enemies with fans of this movie. This is simply my own opinion and not how I feel others should think.

title: This film has NO MATURITY in it!
review:
Why is this stinker rated so high? It stunk on just about every level. Even the special effects! I admit, there was the sense that it took a lot of time and money to do the special effects, but there was nothing groundbreaking about them, and it got to the point of special effects overload. I love science fiction movies, but there must have been a record breaking amount of scenes of alien cities and spaceships landing and taking off. I agree with most of the other bad reviews in that the dialogue was atrocious. The same was true for the last 2 movies before this. The acting and story were bad, as well. A six year old could write a more intelligent story! The proverbial nail in the coffin for me was the wookie doing the "Tarzan" yell while swinging into battle. Not funny or amusing in the least. Also, I don't see the appeal of stupid computer generated yoda.

There were so many groan inducing scenes in this movie, I cannot list them all; it would take too long. I guess that the main thing that bothered me about this movie was its complete lack of maturity or sophistication. This was true in the first 3 movies, but I enjoyed them much more, maybe because I was very young when I saw them. This should not be considered true science fiction. It is more like Disney kiddie fantasy with goofy aliens and silly robots. The "force" is just another name for magic, as well! Also, has dorky Lucas EVER HAD A HOT CHICK IN ANY OF HIS MOVIES??? Is he afraid of them? You could count all the females from all of his Star Wars films on one hand, and none of them were really hot! Whats-her-name was cute at best! Well, I guess the only good thing I can say about this crap-fest is now there shouldn't be any more!

title: It's finally over
review:
I saw Revenge of the Sith when it came out, afterwards I was speechless, it was such a let down, I felt despite their faults Episodes 1 and 2 were building to something. Not only was Episode 3 too violent and not just at the end, but it was numbing, how many light sabre fights can you see before it gets tired? Episode 1's climatic fight was really good, and redeemed the film to an extent (and it had a great theme song), Episode 2's climax had good novelty the first time. Where as what we get is an entire film building up to the most overlong, disappointing duel, the only moment in the entire scene with any resonance was Obi-Wan telling Anakin not to fight him when he has the higher ground. Poor Ewan McGregor: not given a character to work with but a list of mannerisms, poor Christopher Lee: wasted, poor Natalie Portman: badly written. Samuel Jackson could've have been a bit better, although he had three films with nothing to do.

Now that I've seen them all, Episode 1 seems to be the best of the three; at least it has a contained narrative, while 2 and 3 are a complete mess, even if I can see what Lucas was trying to do. Now it's all over I can stop being concerned, the prequels were awful but I still enjoyed them in places, and I was genuinely excited to see all three, even when I read a 1 star review of Revenge of the Sith.

If you're a fan you'll have made your mind up, if not, it's not really worth seeing.

title: Feel cheated? You should be.
review:
The only positive things to say about this "film" are that it is better than either of its two dire predecessors, and that Jar-Jar Binks is barely in it. At least Lucas has listened a little bit.

But what a mess. And all three films are a pointless exercise. Star Wars was the second film I ever saw in the cinema (Jungle Book was the first) and it has stayed with me. Star Wars is fun, Empire Strikes Back is a great film and Return of the Jedi is disappointing but OK.

However, the three "prequels" are shockingly bad. One of the fun things about Star War, as a kid, was the whole mythology that was built up around the film. It starts at full throttle and doesn't really pause. Hints and subtle comments are dropped in throughout the three films, and iterations appear in the right places at the right times.

However, the prequels are definitely a great example of where less is definitely more. What a cheat to have one's images of the "back story" represented as it has been since "Phantom Menace" dribbled out onto the cinema screens. The whole obviousness of the exercise, the nature of the CGI special effects (they are nothing compared to the original film, or the effects in a film such as 2001) and the padding of a concise prelude to Star Wars (it is NEVER Episode IV!) has devalued the originals. Darth Vader is basically a violent version of Harry Enfield's "Kevin The Teenager" character (sorry to non-UK readers of this!). Lucas has taken his seminal creations and covered them in mediocre acting, poor characterisation and hideous dialogue.

In each case we have been told that each film is getting better. They couldn't get worse. Phantom Menace gets my vote as one of the worst ten films ever made, Attack of the Clones is not much better, and Revenge of the Sith is only marginally better than either of them. All those decent actors (McGregor, Jackson, Portman, but NOT the awful Christiansen) must be glad it is over, and they can go and make some decent films again.

At best, all three films could be been fifteen minutes of inserts into the revised 20th Anniversary releases of the original trilogy. Less is more. Look at how real cinematic masters such as Bresson, Bergman and Truffaut et al make such wonderful cinema. They don't spell out every simple twist and turn, and nor did the original trilogy. The "new" trilogy is a dumbed down marketing exercise, with enough scenes in each film to make good templates for PS2 or XBox games. And that's about it. Stick with the wonderful originals and erase the recent travesties - "Sith" included - from your minds.

Mr. Lucas, you have let us all down.

title: I was expecting a good movie...and Lucas let me down...again.
review:
Imagine my hopeful surprise to hear that Revenge of the Sith was gaining wide-spread acceptance in the movie-lovers community. "So much better than Ep 1 and 2!" and "Two thumbs up!" and "Oooh! Dark and Angsty!".

I now know the extent of the Dark Side's power. It blinds people and turns them into annoying fanboys filling the coffers of George Lucas with their hard earned dollars while he wipes his brow with a hearty "Finally...It's over." Well, that's about the only thing I agree with. At least it's over.

I wasn't walking into the theater expecting a masterpiece, but even my limited expectations were thrown out the window during the first half an hour. The pacing of the movie was all wrong. Like a Powerpoint presentation instead of a movie...even going so far as to use the 'blinds' transition and numerous others that raped the original style of Episode 4-6's wipes and smooth scrolls.

Beyond the timing and quick editing, the core of the movie simply isn't that good. A weak plot that was dull even during the action - an obvious side effect to Lucas' lack of joy writing it - only made the style of the movie worse. HURRY! HURRY! HURRY! All to cover up the fact that it really isn't that exciting.

The acting, once again, was terrible. Lucas has the ability to take a perfectly good actor or actress (McGreggor and Portman specifically) and drain them of any kind of charisma and realistic emotion. Only McGreggor as Obiwan seemed to eventually overcome - not to say he didn't suffer at times.

The 'effects' were nice. But even then, I noticed scenes that felt rushed and chopped together. All CGI scenes were amazing, but when the actors needed to be filmed, it seemed like they were secondary to their environments. You can see where the plywood and paint floor ends, and the CGI begins in many scenes.

I was hoping for a lukewarm conclusion. Something that said "Hey, look, at least it's done." Now, I can only thank God that Lucas is done with it. I'm tired of my childhood memories and loves being destroyed by this man.

PS) This movie needed more Wookies.

title: Extra Ordinary Again
review:
Saw this film on 06/04/05, so the "hype" was over by then. There was almost no audience reaction to it, except for 1 scene, where there was some modest laughter.

Most people were yawning, eating munchies or responding to their cells.

Very Ordinary Movie.

Seems just like a replay of the original. Bad acting and all-too-familiar special effects left me wanting for more.

The Light-Saber scenes abound but made no sense.

Would I see this again? No.

Should you pay to rent it? No.

title: Hear that sound of a deflating balloon?
review: I'm REALLY disappointed. Taken as a stand-alone film, it's enjoyable nonsense; taken as the crucial link between the prequels and the original three episodes, it's frankly First Grade essay level. The dialogue is poor, Christensen again fails to convince except right at the end, and (very impressive) CGI is used too much to cover up the shortcomings. I wanted so much to have my faith restored after Ep. 1 and 2, but even ROTJ is better than this, and to say that the one with Ewoks is better sums up how disappointing this is. How is it that Anakin can decide to give up his years of Jedi training and switch to the Sith within one scene? There should have been more time spent on showing his emotional problems - Darth Vader is after all THE MOST EVIL villain - and they actually could have left out the Wookies altogether. There is more than enough of Chewbacca in the original films. And how do the Jedi all die so easily if they can use the Force to fly around etc.? Actually why do the troops suddenly turn on the Jedi when these guys have been protecting the Republic for so long? Some positive words, since I gave the film 5 out of 10: Ewan McGregor is good, Natalie Portman does her best with what she's given, and the planets are beautifully rendered. C3P0 is a bit player, which reduces the ham factor a bit, and there's no Jar-Jar. Christopher Lee makes the most of his few minutes on screen, and Ian McDiarmid is excellent as Palpatine. What a shame that the overall result comes up short. Mr. Lucas - there's only one thing you can do to redeem yourself now. Re-shoot the battle scenes in TESB with the latest CGI and take out the (impossible) sound effects in the space scenes. Then re-release it; it's still the best of the 6 by miles (in no small part thanks to Harrison Ford), and an upgrade on the FX would make it simply stunning. DO NOT even think about making any new ones. Enough is enough. Actually it would have been better in retrospect to have just had the first 3, but too late now! Nerd point: I may be wrong but I'm sure I saw the Millennium Falcon landing in the distance in one of the early scenes.

title: Another disappointment...
review:
Anakin's motivations for turning to the dark side and his subsequent actions make no sense. I think Lucas developed the character of Anakin in the prior two movies and ended up writing himself into a corner. The following situation would be a similar situation in today's world.

"An up-and-coming American general involved in the war against terror has a sick wife at home. Amazingly, he discovers that his next door neighbor is really Osama Bin Laden. When he discovers this, Osama tells him that he has a cure for his wife's illness and that he will give it to him, but in order to do this he will have to start working for him. His first duty is to divert some nuclear warheads and send them to secret terrorist cells in all of America's large cities. His second is to arrange for all the leaders to be in those cities. And last, he is to give the codes to set these weapons off. Of course this would destroy everything he has ever known, cause an amazing amount of suffering, and be against everything he has ever believed, but at least his wife might live a little bit longer." It just doesn't make sense...

title: A Lost Opportunity
review:
The Prequel Trilogy is complete. It has been an experience... but not the experience that I had hoped. Now I suppose, my expectations of the new Star Wars movies may have been set a bit too high (but then again weren't all of ours), but after watching the last of the new movies I can say without a doubt that this Prequel Trilogy contains three of the worst movies I have ever seen.

George Lucas had such an opportunity to expand on the mythology of the original trilogy, it's character's, their origin, but also the galaxy of Star Wars. The promise was to see the whole arcing story of Anakin Skywalker. From good, seduced by evil, and returning to the light side of the force. Well we got that, but it was done in such a way that it makes more sense to watch the Original Trilogy then the Prequel Trilogy to fill in the back story. It would almost make more sense to re-cut (again) the Original Trilogy and add in footage from the Prequel Trilogy as flashbacks or montages. It would be a lot more entertaining than watching the new three movies. If these movies had been released without the Star Wars name, they would have tanked, simple as that.

Remember watching the Original Trilogy, and the shock of discovering that Darth Vader was the father of Luke and Leia. Now think of showing all 6 movies to your children, or someone who hasn't seen Star Wars before. They watch the originals and after much begging, you convince them that the final 3 are much better and they should watch them. They finish the 2nd Trilogy, and wonder why there was so much emphasis put on the scene where Darth Vader reveals that he is Luke's father, they already knew that Anakin was Darth Vader and Luke and Leia's father. Then they start asking questions, like why does Leia have memories of her mother (Return of the Jedi, when Leia and Luke talking on Endor), when Padme dies immediately after childbirth (for absolutely NO reason). From my point of view, one of the most important things the Prequel trilogy needed to avoid was redundancy in the plot. Showing us that Luke and Leia are brother and sister makes Luke's revelation that Leia is his sister completely pointless for the audience, just like the reveal that Vader is his father. Also, depending on which version of the Original Trilogy you show them, why does Anakin's ghost look like the young Anakin not the old one (and to everyone who rationalizes it by saying that you see the spirit as the person was when they were part of the light side, Anakin did save Luke and kill the Emperor, returning him to the Light Side). And how does Obi Wan know in A New Hope that Darth Vader is Anakin? As far as he knows by the end of Sith, Anakin died on the volcano world. Is the identity of Vader common knowledge in the Empire?

From what's gone up on the screen, it doesn't seem Lucas put any thought into the fundamentals of what he needed to do in the Prequels. The inevitable conclusion that I reach is that this Trilogy was made to sell more Star Wars toys to a new generation of kids and not to set up an exciting base for the Original Trilogy, one that could stand on it's own. It's a missed opportunity of massive proportions, but fortunately, from what Lucas has been saying, he will never make another Star Wars movie again.

title: Too bad Lucas didn't seem to care about telling the story
review: Star Wars has always been good because it is a story of mythological proportions, filled with potential for analogy and interpretation. The last two of Lucas's films have severely disappointed most audiences in this regard, pandering to children with unnecessary silliness while attempting to capture teenage and older audiences with technical mastery -- forgetting that it was the story as much as the special effects that gave the trilogy its magic. The Revenge of the Sith, while having some of the best potential of the three in terms of plot, with loads of political scheming and important characters pitted against each other and undergoing personal transformation, fails to pay attention to the story itself. Lucas neglects storytelling in order to play with on-screen digital wizardry. The effect is often dazzling, but dazzling like a psychedelic light show: fabulous moving shapes and flashes, but with no meaning. The characters are reduced to hollow husks, such that the blurring between human and machine that has always been at the heart of Star Wars symbolism matters little to us, characters are cartoon images of themselves and they dissolve like the 1 and 0s they are made up of when they are killed off. Lucas is so eager to show us the myriad worlds he has conjured up that he doesn't really give us a chance to see them, their names come and go so quickly that they fade from memory and blur into one another. While Tattouine and Endor were sources of inspiration for my childhood imagination, I have trouble believing that any but the Lava planet (whatever it was called) will stick with this generation. And the efficacy of that planet partly stemmed from its reminiscence of Mordor. Ultimately, this is why the Lord of the Rings so easily dominated what should have been an equally legendary set of films, because those films used special effects to aid the telling of a story. Lucas gave his computer toys precedence and produced something that is sadly kind of boring.

title: The Force was not really in it..
review:
This film is a must see, simply because it is the link in the saga, but that is about where it ends.

First off, the special effects are stunning. A small army of people worked on them and these did a very nice job. The problem is that there is hardly any shot *without* SFX and cross-fades are at a high pace. It seems likes Lucas is racing towards the finish and moving in full force to do so. Everyone is an action hero, including R2D2, and the Jedi are put to use as one-man armies.

Unfortunately, the film suffers from three flaws. Most annoyingly, there seems to be no chemistry between Hayden Christensen (Anakin) and Natalie Portman (Padme), whose characters are supposed to be in love. In fact, the latter connects much more with Ewan McGregor (Obi-Wan), who was surely the best actor in the film.

The second flaw is the pomp in general. Whereas the early Star Wars films still seemed like they were fun, the later (and this one in particular) are heavier in drama and music than a Wagner opera.

The third is that Anakin is walking into a rather obvious trap set by Darth Sidious, and somehow gives a Sith Lord the benefit of the doubt over all of his Jedi mentors, in the face of much too blatant political maneuvering.

All in all, I feel Lucas overshot his target. The film is more action than adventure, as if the video game knockoff was the most important consideration. My suspension of disbelief was long gone by the time Darth Vader rose in his dark suit.

None of this matters, of course, because hordes will go and see it, if only for that scene and the accompanying music.

P.S. One more thing: personally, I deeply regretted that Jar Jar Binks did not get killed.

title: Lucas missing the mark, and managing to prove himself a shallow and overblown 'artist.'
review:
Although I disliked Christensen's performance as well, and for that matter the entirety of the acting portions of the movie, I think there is far more wrong with Revenge of the Sith than simply a B-level heartthrob's poorly directed performance. The directing in its encompassing touch on the film could be to blame. This will not be only an assault on Mr. Lucas's credibility and integrity as an artist, but I must work to highlight the good parts of this as a film, the best of the prequels (although that is not to say much).

In Phantom Menace and Attack of the Clones, there was a layer of crusted, old, worn-out, and unnecessary cheese caked on in a rather thick amount, with C-3PO's head being dragged in an unrealistic slapstick setup then coming to utter the line, "what a drag," and have vanish with it the last bit of salvageable respect I could possibly have for the jiggly-necked Lucas and his work. I had thought the value of the first three films, as they were originally released and received by the world, could not be insulted to a greater degree than what Jar Jar Binks did for the legacy of an American classic. Even though my viewing of this film happened in a packed theater with the movie-going sheep hooting and clapping at the slightest bit of physical comedy (and I dare say unfunny comedy at best) brought to a scene, I did find there to be a lack of such situations past the first fifteen minutes of screen time. The cattle I had the pleasure of viewing the film with would even laugh and applaud at moments when there wasn't a deliberate move by Lucas to drum a rise from the mass crowd. Yet, despite collective humanity's greatest attempts to ruin by annoyance the 'pleasure' of seeing this film for the first time, there was nowhere near as much of the outright crap within this feature.

To find the real crap, you have to look deeper. Maybe only a few inches deeper, but elements of character attributes, metaphors, double-entendres, overlying themes, and true and passionately motivated characters are absent from this film, leaving little in the way of layers through which to dig.

However, there is the use of political unrest modeled after relevant scenarios that seems to strike a contemporary meaningful note. The setup being built based on the circumstances of the Vietnam War, yet ringing true with importance to today (demonstrating how history perhaps repeats itself...who'da thunkit). This one bit of significance cannot be used to establish credit for Lucas, for he employed it with little detail or methods of reflection, and all of the inspired thoughts one can have weighing Palpatine's line, "we will destroy the Jedi, and then we will have peace," are more so attributable to the reality of the application of that line today and not to the use within the film.

Perhaps Lucas's greatest failing did revolve around Christensen, though. As I sit and ponder the spectacle I have just witnessed (I'm writing this at 3am on return from seeing the film) I find myself realizing that the depths Anakin reaches so quickly came from no motivation other than the obligatory plot line created within A New Hope. The changes that the characters in Revenge of the Sith find themselves going through seem to come from the same necessity, and nothing else. Anakin sways to the dark side to learn the power to save Padme, and then quickly moves to taking a sadistic pleasure in slaughtering children? It doesn't work. And that about says it for this film. For me, there will always be an entirely dis-interesting quality possessed by works of art that exhibit a complete lack of ambiguity. Beyond that, Revenge of the Sith seemed to be a dying whimper of creativity that marks (perhaps most importantly) the end of Lucas's obligation to us, the viewing public, to finish his behemoth of a project that all started with a passion, a vision, and a Joseph Campbell novel. If there is anything that this film accomplished, then it is that and nothing more.

title: Laughably bad writing, direction and acting
review:
I was hoping for a grand end of the prequel trilogy of my favorite movies when I was growing up. I still remember being a 10 year old kid sitting in the Colosseum movie theater in Oslo being totally at awe in watching Return of the Jedi back in 1983. It has always been the greatest movie experience of my life and it always will be. I now think that Empire is even better (I was too young to see it in 1980) and have bought the original trilogy on VHS, Laserdisc and DVD (and I will buy them when they come to Blu-ray). This prequel trilogy was just such a waste. All the talent in front of and behind the camera, except Lucas, was wasted on these movies. I have written a review on the first prequel movie and I must say now that I feel even worse about it, episode 2 and this movie. I have seen all three of the prequel movies several times now and I must say that they contain so much clichés that it is almost frightening. I cannot say how many times I cringe when I see these horrors that are disguised as Star Wars movies. When I see the pod race in the first movie I keep thinking that I am seeing a sort of desert live-action Wipe-Out race.

But I will keep my comments to this movie. All aspects of the movie are such drivel. The worst things are the script and the direction, both by Lucas. The last movie George Lucas directed before episode 1 is the 1977 Star Wars. That's over 20 years of not directing any movie. His third time around he is still bad. It seems like the movie is all over the place. I read another review on this site and he was totally right when he wrote that the wipes were all over the place. This bad editing is the result of a bad script that needed trimming and believability. Not to mention the truly horrible dialog.

What everyone was waiting for, Anakin's seduction into the dark side, was done so badly. Hayden Christensen's ham acting didn't help, but with a superior director (basically any of Hollywood's good directors would do a better job) the acting could have been improved on. When Anakin kills Count Dooku in the beginning of the movie I keep thinking "That's it? No more remorse about killing another human being in cold blood?". We see no conscience at work at all. Anakin's seduction by Palpatine to the dark side is also very unbelievably done. When Anakin cuts off Windu's arm Palpatine screams "Power! Unlimited power!!" and throws lightning at him so he is thrown far into the city. Can't Anakin see him for what he is, a manipulative, deceitful evil man that is behind everything that has transpired all his life? No. All he says is "What have I done?". Everything Palpatine has been pretending to care about has been a lie. His mentor is the very evil he has been fighting all his life. Does he reject him because of this? No. OK. He wants to save Padme's life, but how can he know that this ability about saving people from death wasn't a lie too? The transformation from good to bad is done so badly. It was very cool to hear the great James Earl Jones as the voice of Darth Vader when he put on the famous suit, but I cringed at the the dialog spoken. The romance between Anakin and Padme is also handled like a bad high school play with acting and dialog to match. The technical side of the movie is second to none. The effects and sound design are really great.

When I was a teenager I kept thinking about how Anakin Skywalker had turned to evil since he was really a good person. How can a good person willingly do all these terrible things? He was my favorite villain of all and he still is. I think I have to pretend like these horrible prequel movies never was made. I just hope that the original trilogy will appear on Blu-ray in their original incarnations and not with all the out-of-place digital CGI work what were inserted into the movies back in 1997. This movie was just a letdown that I think it is better to think that it and the two previous movies weren't made at all.

title: A fitting end to an awful trilogy...
review:
And so we arrive at the end of Star Wars episodes one to three, a scornful and exploitative six to nine hour merchandising marathon the likes of which we will be lucky to never see again.

The bitterness of the above statement says a great deal about how betrayed I feel by George Lucas and his team, most specifically Rick McCallum, whose sound bites really brought home the cynicism with which the Star Wars prequels were made. My 'favourite' will forever be: 'The Phantom Menace succeeded as a film,' followed closely by: 'Jar Jar Binks did his job as a character.' I may have misquoted him a little but the gist of his perspective was quite clear.

Needless to say I did not like this movie. There are many reasons, some of which stem from the film itself and others from the trilogy as a whole. On the former side: this film is too long, too frenetic, has appalling blending of CGI with real people, lacks any decent acting, boasts a truly diabolical script, is without any sense of cohesion, offers some stunningly bad explanations for certain key events and is fairly incompatible with the original trilogy... and that's just off the bat.

In terms of the entire trilogy the problems with the whole are legion and not dissimilar to the list above. The script, acting, CGI, characters, cohesion, incompatibility and preposterous ideas inflicted on us, the paying audience, were just one insult after another. However, most diabolical of all must be the Star Wars marketing and merchandising.

The original Star Wars was never expected to make any money nor even to succeed. When it did its creator gained a lot of cash, especially because Fox gave up all the merchandising rights. Lucas subsequently exploited our love of the films in a way second only to Disney for sheer cynicism, though the damage was initially contained due to his minimal involvement in Empire and Jedi. This can best be summed up as follows: in recent years the House of Mouse have given us films like Jungle Book 2. George Lucas gave us the Star Wars prequels.

From the off it seemed like these films were only made to make money. There was little sense of love or, more importantly, pride in them at all. Everything was up for grabs... from child friendly characters to the cool toys on offer that any Star Wars fan instantly wanted to own. Story and other minor details were swept under the carpet in favour of situations which put young dollars in close proximity to expensive products.

For us, the fans of the original trilogy, it was one long, poisonous screeching of greedy fingernails along the blackboards of our souls. We desperately wanted a trilogy that had all the warmth, love, affection, sass and inspiration of the original. Instead all we got was a giant catalogue for Star Wars products, games and other tie ins.

Revenge of the Sith is just as guilty as the rest of them. In between chaotic space battles, touchy feely lightsabre fights, cackling bad guys and monotonous good ones, there is a constant bombardment of purchasable items. See a computer generated Yoda take on a computer enhanced Palpatine... and buy their weapons, clothes, prosthetics, voice boxes, hats, shoes, belts, spacecraft, lunch boxes, breakfast cereals, yo-yo's, boomerangs, inflatable castles, action figures and everything else. That's just two characters and one tenth of the stuff available to each of them.

For those of you who rightly say that this review fails to offer any explanation as to why I think the films are so bad I must admit that I am guilty, breaking one of my own rules for this website. However, the myriad of problems with ROTS and the other prequels are too much to discuss without settling down for several hours.

I had huge hopes for this film... and Attack of the Clones... and most of all for the Phantom Menace, having been assaulted by such a barrage of advertising and such like that said 'YES! WE FINALLY HAVE A DECENT NEW STAR WARS FILM!' Unfortunately, like all the rest of them, that hope has soured into the bitterest of disappointments and has left me hoping that, come the new Star Wars TV series, I simply won't be in a position to see them and further add to my disillusionment.

title: The worst of the Star Wars films
review:
I came to Episode 3 full of hope. After two less than brilliant entries into the franchise, I thought mistakes would be fixed, ideas freshened and all loose ends tied up. I was wrong. I have seen better story lines in video games and professional wrestling, only they come with more interesting characters.

Like a car crash on screen, I knew what was going to happen. I knew it was going to be messy. I knew there would be pain. But I kept looking. Why did I keep looking? Why did George Lucas take my hand in his, with a gun in his other one, pointing at me? Why, George, why?

I hated all the characters, if 'character' could accurately be used to describe the CGI-generated bipeds on screen (although I'm told some human actors were used, but I couldn't tell which they were, due to the terrible acting). They were hollow shells, a facade, a covering for something that wasn't there inside, like a Kinder Surprise, but without the pleasing toy contained within.

Harrison Ford once said to George Lucas, "you can write this $h*t George, but you can't say it." At least in those days he had Harrison Ford to deliver the lines. Now everything spoken by the characters seems to have been taken out of the Big Book Of Bad Guy Clichés and Stan Lee's Guide To How Superheros Should Talk.

I'm getting angry now, so I'll stop. God, this film is terrible. To summarise:

Plot: Thinner than an bulimic pancake Characters: Less sympathetic than a mass murdering head cheerleader CGI: Pretty, but vacuous, like a mass murdering head cheerleader Dialogue: More corny than a poorly-maintained foot

Thank God Episode 4 is A New Hope. We need it after this.

title: George Lucas can now be crowned The Legend Slayer
review:
Why the movie sucked: 1. Natalie Portman did a horrible acting job. 2. Hayden Christianwhatever was worse than a bad actor in a high school play. 3. The dialogue was so bad that I found myself as well as other moviegoers in the theater laughing my @ss off. 4. Lucas (The Legend Slayer) used way too much special effects. Was I watching the last installment of a classic or a 2 hour resume for Lucas's special effects people. 5. Anakin's fall to the darkside was like flipping a switch. 6. This movie was loaded with inconsistencies: a) R2D2 can fly? b) I thought the jedi were bad @ss warriors. Why were they dispatched so easily. c) Padme seemed awfully small for someone with twins. d) In the first Star Wars princess Leia says something to the effect of knowing her mother a little when she was very young - I guess she was not talking about Padme either that or her memory is so good she can remember things when she was 3 seconds old. e) General Grievious's was beaten way to easily by Obi Wan. 7. Is Lucas, The Legend Slayer, fixated on people hanging from very tall heights. How many times in all 3 prequels was Obi Wan hanging off of something during a big fight scene (Darth Maul, Jango Fett, General Grievious). How many times was Anakin? This got old very quick. Is George Lucas capable of originality, after all he did create the Star Wars universe. 8. Yoda's facial expressions were laughable. I liked yoda better in the original series, when he was a puppet. 9. The scene where Papaltine is using the darkside on Samuel Jackson and trying to talk in an evil voice was completely hysterical. 10. There still was no chemistry between Hayden and Natalie.

There were a couple of good things about the movie but not nearly enough to warrant the rave reviews by critics and certainly not enough for Revenge of the Sith to earn a spot on IMDBs top 250 list.

I predict that over the next 6 months, if not sooner, people will come to there senses and Revenge of the Sith will be seen for what it really is, a C movie with A++ special effects.

I would now like to address all the critics that were rating this movie an A/A-. You did a great disservice to your profession. I was not going to see this movie because the last two were so bad, however after hearing about the great reviews and reading several I changed my mind and went to see it. Thnaks to all your reviews I shall not rely on critic reviews anymore and I will spread the word that reviews are now extremely unreliable for an accurate, honest, and unbiased take on a movie.

title: Pretty Poor Indeed
review: Should Lucas be allowed to mess with his own films? Well that certainly went far enough when he meddled with 4-6 , quite glad I've still got each of them on original VHS from before 1997 even if they're a little tired , But even that doesn't compare to the dross that is Episodes 1-3 and Revenge of the Sith merely finishes this insult off , and finally gives me the closure to disregard and forget all these prequels and be left with just the memory of the original 3 films even if it involves fuzzy lines and fiddling with the tracking . Altogether what lets this film down is not terrible acting or a bad storyline , it just simply is rushed and poorly executed by someone who is clearly not a good director , remember the best Star Wars Film by far was not directed by Lucas , and I agree with one other user that the turn to the dark side was more like an instantaneous flip to the dark side with no real progression or thought for actions , indeed another user points to the Godfather where Michael gradually becomes involved to protect his father but this is done with some consideration for the steps involved in such a transformation .

title: insult on my intelligence
review:
I expected nothing (wasn't so fond of the previous two) so I came with brain on zero just hoping to enjoy the special effects or something, but this one really insults my intelligence. Even trying not to pay attention, the inconsistencies in the plot are overwhelming.

There is not much of a soundtrack, you just hear robot noises, the performance of the actors are at most mediocre. I don't want to imagine the money invested in the special effects. Compared to the result it must be a waste of money. The screen is filled with elements but there is nothing harmonic about it.

My recommendation would be to skip this one and try to savor the good memory of the older star wars movies.

title: I wish I was shot in a war
review: Star Wars III: Revenge of the Sith. It seemed like the greatest movie through the incredible trailer. I attend a 9 o'clock show and fell asleep right in the theater, even after drinking about 10 Cokes at my friend's house, along with a box of Sno-Caps. It was like watching C-Span for two and a half hours. It kept switching back and forth from a good 5-minute battle to a 30-minute discussion with Samuel L. Jackson on Palpatine's plan to overthrow the Counsel. I wanted to go into the movie screen, grab Anakin's light saber, and kill myself. THe only good thing in the movie was Yoda's battle, it was like watching Kermit the Frog beat the s*** out of the puppeteers controlling him. Star Wars is a stinker, go see The Longest Yard or Kicking and Screaming, if you prefer ESPN to CNN.

title: best of new three, still not up to par.
review:
As a fan, I wanted to suspend disbelief for this movie, but it just wasn't possible. I had to shake my head at several scenes in the movie, especially Anakins turn to the dark side. And what was up with the lava surfing scene? I am disappointed in IMDb users who give this a ten. You are wearing your "fan" goggles too much, or you were drunk from all of the alcohol you imbibed while waiting days in line. There are maybe only 20 or so movies that deserve a ten. Mr Lucas was involved in none of them.

Pros: Special Effects, Action Cons: Dialogue, Editing, Humor. Hayden (SP?) Christian Bale would have made an awesome Anakin. Next time make me in charge of casting.

title: Monetary motivation leads to the Dark Side, and George turned a long time ago.
review:
I won't say I absolutely hated it. At least it kept me awake and entertained (when I wasn't cringing or laughing out loud at the wrong moments). But sometime after Return of the Jedi, Lucas either lost or gave up his abilities to write and direct. Phantom Menace and Attack of the Clones both proved that to this die-hard fan who was a 4-year-old when A New Hope was released. Star Wars was a big part of my childhood. I feel depressed about the way these prequels were handled. All three could have been so much better.

Flashy action scenes and great CGI alone, do not a great film make. What's saddest to me is that while this film was supposed to be about Anakin/Vader, the best scenes were Palpatine's. That character's progression from Senator to Emperor was the only high point in this prequel trilogy, story-wise. The rest was choppy, graceless, often needless, horribly cheesy, and in some cases (especially with Padme's death in this film), contradictory to the original trilogy.

I would like to blame acting, but honestly, even Oscar-winners cannot be convincing when given shoddy material. While I might have preferred a somewhat older and more mature actor for Anakin in this film, Hayden did do far better this time than in Attack of the Clones. But the writing made it almost impossible for the actor to stand a chance at being a convincing Darth Vader. And the lovers' scenes were nauseatingly stupid due to (once again) lazy writing, as well as a total lack of chemistry between the players. Padme seemed too matronly, and Anakin too much a horndog.

But hey, if you like lots of great light-saber fights and cameo appearances by names and old favorites and wicked cool bird-beaked-lizards (that creature was the best thing about the CGI), by all means, enjoy! Like I said, I won't say I hated it. The previous prequels prepared me for shallow effects being the only enjoyable thing, and I got what I paid for. But it's still disappointing knowing George Lucas could have done so much better, but instead chose the high-paid, I-can't-go-wrong-with-the-Star-Wars-name, ego-trip.

I wonder if he even watched his old films before writing this screenplay?

title: Why do the "critics" love this movie??
review:
zzz ..... Oh wait the movie is over and I can wake up. This movie was horrible!! I can't tell you how many times I checked my watch. It is a sad ending to the original Star Wars movies.

The worse part of this movie was the acting. Could Hayden Christensen show one ounce of charisma or screen presence or acting skill? It appears that he can not. Since the movie focused around his turn to the dark side, it required an actor that could take over a movie and make it his own. Obviously they picked the wrong guy.

I don't understand all the gushing from the critics. Did they see a different movie then the rest of us? If you must see this movie do it in the theaters so at least you can enjoy the special effects. Just wait until it reaches the cheap theaters. Definitely not worth full price!!

title: Lost Chance
review:
This is a film that grants Spy Kids a run for its money.

Stripped of its position in the Star Wars story arc, Episode 3 would be average Hollywood fair. Given the iconic status Star Wars has carved for itself in Western culture, however, this movie is simply disappointing.

Darth Vader is part of the fabric of our modern mythos. He is a legend. For once the director does not have to make us fear the villain, because we already do. This is coming from someone who is not really a fan of the original series. I am not a Star Wars fanatic, but they are part of my culture, and with that comes a certain amount of respect. It is a sentiment that is sadly not shared by the production team.

The villain in this movie is a McDonald's-Happy-Meal version of his original self. He is no longer a cold, calculating being, but a coldly calculated one. His Empire will not control planets, but malls.

Not everything in this movie is terrible. In fact, far from it. The production values on the whole are good. The effects are excellent (if distracting and overused). What is totally lacking is relevance and emotion. It's sad really. I would have liked to see what a better director could do with this material.

3/10

title: Nobody could possibly expect it to be that bad
review:
All right, just returned from the cinema. Frankly, I didn't expect much of it. I went to watch it for the main reason that I've seen all SW movies around the time they came out so I wanted to watch the last one as well. But - what I didn't expect was that mind-numbing assault of unbelievably bad crap. The acting was in a galaxy far, far below any known standard, the dialogue made me grind my teeth (it was a true rival for the abysmal Blade III) and George Lucas' idea of tying up loose ends to connect EP III with IV is something very much like what a six-year old boy would think up. Every time Hayden Christensen attempted to put on an evil or angry facial expression I was forced to summon all strength not to explode with laughter. I could go on now for about an hour but I'll spare the eventual readers of this comment and myself the time. In summary, the movie was a waste of money.

I honestly don't understand how more than 48% of the voters could give 10 points. 2/10 from me for the special effects which were extremely well made but this can't save a movie that lacks everything else.

title: Don't Give George Lucas your money EVER!!!
review:
I give this a 2 and not a 1 just because the ghost of Alec Guinness deserves better.

I won't give away spoilers. Just these few thoughts.

1. HORRIBLE DIALOGUE!!! And that for these last three in general. No Wit. No "Laugh it up fuzz ball" or "I don't know, fly casual." Just lots of "You rebel scum!" Sure that's a funny line, but a whole movie of that!!! Awful.

2. I thought a turn to the Dark Side was pretty intense. Guess what it isn't. Remember when Vader told Luke if he wouldn't turn to the dark side, maybe his sister would? Remember how intense that was!!! Well this isn't.

3. Poorly filled plot holes, enough said about that.

4. Kevin Smith was wrong about Hayden Christiansen. (spell check) He is bad. which brings me to my last point.

5. I don't really blame the actors, they did the best with what they had. George Lucas has no idea how to write. Why were Empire and Jedi so good? George didn't write those two by himself NOR DID HE DIRECT THEM!!!!! That man should be taken away, far far away.

Hopfully some one will rise in about 20 years and remake these movies, but good. I am saddened that kids today think this is StarWars. Did you notice how very infrequently they said "May The Force Be With You?" Remember how the first 3 movies were all about internal struggle and not about the special effects? I saw nothing in this movie that makes me want to see it again. The trailer, again, was better.

title: First Viewing, early impressions
review: 'Revenge' is the film that justifies the existence of the first two mediocre episodes because without them you can't fully appreciate this tragedy on the grandest scale. I don't think its a spoiler to say that the whole thing ends pretty badly but it is infinitely more entertaining then watching a little kid race pods and so forth. It also has incredible visuals that really dwarf the first two installments much like ROTK did with LOTR (lots of acronyms!) Based on my first impression, I rate this as the second best installment of the six films, slightly behind EMPIRE but this is so much darker and heavier than even that film that I may be inclined to change my mind and call this one the centerpiece of the whole spectacle. Then again I'm still in a daze from seeing it so I could be wrong...

title: as bad as it gets
review: the last time i was so disappointed with a movie, it had vin diesel in it. lucas wasn't even trying with 'revenge of the sith'. the story did not measure up to the first three, the cgi was second-rate at best, and the story was weak from the start. like episodes 1 and 2, this movie had loads of potential, but failed to deliver at every step. die hards will see this movie and probably not complain too much, but the casual star wars fan will recognize how truly bad this movie is. the movie had few moments that were classic. like the way yoda escaped after his fight with palpating (i won't tell you, but it reminds you of something in empire strikes back.) yoda was the best part of this movie. sadly, that's just not saying much. in short, when a movie is this bad, it spurs you. it makes you want to get on the internet and tell everyone just how bad it is. its not that they made a bad movie that ticks me off. the problem is that they made a bad movie and they are still going to clean up at the box office.

title: An excellent movie
review:
The wait is finally over and we get to see the end of the star wars saga...and in my opinion it was well worth the wait.

This movie is the best of the prequels and has a lot of action in it, even Ewan McGregor said "its ridiculous how much action there is in this movie". This movie is about anakin skywalkers fall to the dark side and it was very well done and convincing to me. There are lightsaber duels aplenty in this star wars movie, 5 in total and that is more than any other star wars movie. The best of these has to be Anakin and Obi-Wan's lightsaber duel, with the actors having to go through months of training before shooting to make it look good.

There are only a few possible flaws in this movie (that is only if I am nitpicking) but these don't make the movie bad...if one looks hard enough it is possible to find flaws in any movie! This last chapter in the star wars saga is very dark, just as dark if not darker than the empire strikes back (episode V). The saga is now complete and what a saga it has been, this series of movies are my favourite movies and I think all the star wars movies (including revenge of the sith) are very good.

title: concluding an awful exposition of the original trilogy.
review:
In my opinion this film is the worst of all three prequel trilogies, everything wrong with the first two is in abundance here. Every line of spoken dialogue in the original trilogy has suffered an exposition in the prequel trilogy which only serves to sully enjoyment of the original films. There are incestuous and needless relationships between characters and far too many self-referential moments which seem to serve no other purpose than remind viewers of a really good film a long, long time ago. The CGI is distracting and not necessary to tell the story, and despite advances, does not look real. The acting is terrible and emotionless. The film is too long.

But my real criticism is that in attempting to explain and show everything in the Star Wars galaxy it leaves the viewer no room to imagine or think for themselves. That's how I felt watching it - slowly my own interpretation of the original trilogy being replaced by one big CGI mess with poor story and acting. But perhaps this was inevitable.

title: Heartbreaking
review:
I have been dying to see this film since I heard Lucas was making Episode I. I've always been a big fan of the Star Wars series. Not a true fan, for I'm not really obsessed like most fans, but I've a moderate Star Wars collection and a knowledge of the Star Wars universe that won me first place in 'Who wants to be a Jedi Master' at a Con called Fanfair. LOL! Anyway, the first two films. The Phantom Menace and Attack Of The Clones were not the best Lucas could have done, and didn't really top the original films. They held their own to me, but Revenge Of The Sith falls right into place with Episodes 4, 5, and 6. We all knew that this film was to be very serious with the rise of the empire and Anakin's decent to the dark side. However, I was worried it would be watered down for younger viewers. However, Lucas didn't pull any punches. I was almost crying and I only held it in because I didn't want to get teased by my friends. Huge Spoiler if you haven't seen it yet. If you don't mind Spoilers ... keep reading.

There are some quite disturbing parts, like where Anakin kills off the youngest Jedi in the Main Council Chamber. Even though they don't actually show him kill the 'younglings', you know what happens, and it's heartbreaking.

The Clones who are fighting side by side with the Jedi against the Droid Army are given a message by Palpatine. They then turn on the unsuspecting Jedi who in short are shot in the back. These scenes will make your jaw drop. They did mine. The light-saber battles featuring General Grievous and Yoda (no they didn't fight each other, I mean different fight scenes) were quite spectacular. Both had a unique style of fighting with sabers. I won't spoil the outcome of those fights or who they end up fighting.

Padme's situation in the movie is the most heartbreaking. Being pregnant at this time, (I'm actually due this month, LOL!) I was really touched by her situation. It's really heartbreaking how Luke and Leia are born, Padme dies, and Anakin becomes the Vader we know at the same time.

You won't be disappointed when you see this film, but you might be slightly disturbed by how dark things are in the end. Prepare yourself.

title: Much better than the previous two, the next ones are still better!
review:
"Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith" (USA, 2005, 140 Min., Theatrical Version)

A Review by Jonathan Fain

[7/10]

The closer the story line gets to the original Star Wars trilogy, the better the movie is. The mixture of the classic Star Wars storyline, and the bad tasted prequel story is excused due to the keep-on improving Computer Graphics, which steals the attention from the mess it creates in the story.

I like Special Effects, also CGI, but watching this film and its prequels is like watching a computer game movie. Towards the ending of the film, themes from the original trilogy begin to appear: Darth Vader's black mask, The Imperial Soldiers and white halled battleships, and everything seems to become aesthetic, so is the story.

The movie is full of action. At one point I grew tedious of the numerous light saber duels, and thanked god for they stopped fighting and started a dialog, which was beginning to be more interesting. The spaceship battle scenes are gigantic and too detailed and messy, makes it hard to follow the action.

In my opinion, this movie should open the saga and the fans should discard the 2 prequels, as they were truly not related to the magic of the Star Wars world.

Every kid that goes to this film, will understand the meaning of DEMOCRACY, as the term is repeated several times throughout the film. It is important for a film to teach, however, how bluntly the characters spill those words off the screen, it's annoying. Let us not forget the extremely poor, and cheesy "Love Dialogs" between Anakin and Padme. It started to annoy me in the previous episode already. The love dialogs between Han Solo to Princess Lea in the classic Star Wars were in funny and exciting and much more human.

All of the characters receive closure except for the one character who made the original Star Wars a blockbuster, and I mean HAN SOLO. He is the reason why Star Wars was such a great movie. This movie doesn't mention Solo at all.

Although the movie has many flaws, it creates a closure to the entire Star Wars plot, which gives to this movie a Shakespearean or maybe biblical atmosphere (especially at the last 5 minutes). The ending was exciting. Although I suffered at some parts of the movie with the messy and repetitive action, the ending got me out of the theater with a taste for more. Well, I do have the original trilogy at home... guess I can continue the adventure. Thank you George Lucas.

"Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith" (USA, 2005, 140 Min., Theatrical Version) | Genre: Action, Adventure, Fantasy, Romance, Sci-Fi | Director: George Lucas 7 out 10.
